translation_en: Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “By Him in whose hand Muhammad’s soul is, I am the closest of people to every believer on earth. If one of you leaves a debt or dependents, come to me, for I am his protector; if he leaves property, it belongs to his male-line relatives.” The chain is Muhammad ibn Rafi, Shababah, Warqa, Abu al-Zinad, and al-Araj.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “I have the closest claim to the believers according to the Book of Allah. If any of you leaves a debt or dependents, call me, for I am his guardian. Whoever leaves property, let his male-line relatives inherit it.” Hammam ibn Munabbih related this report through Abd al-Razzaq and Maamar.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet said: “Whoever leaves property, it belongs to the heirs; whoever leaves dependents, they are our responsibility.” This report was transmitted by Ubayd Allah ibn Muadh, his father, Shu‘bah, Adi, Abu Hazim, and Abu Hurairah.

This is another chain from Shu‘bah, through Abu Bakr ibn Nafi and Ghundar, and Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. Ghundar’s version says: “Whoever leaves dependents, I will take care of them.”

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: “I gave a fine horse in the path of Allah, but the man neglected it. I thought he might sell it cheaply, so I asked the Messenger of Allah about buying it. He said: ‘Do not buy it or take back your charity. The one who takes back his charity is like a dog returning to its vomit.’”
This is the same report through another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb reported it from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Malik. It adds: “Do not buy it, even if he offers it to you for one dirham.”

Umar said he gave a horse in the path of Allah and later found it with its owner, who had neglected it and was poor. Umar wanted to buy it and asked the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Do not buy it, even for one dirham. The one who takes back his charity is like a dog returning to its vomit.” The account is transmitted by Umayyah ibn Bistam, Yazid ibn Zuray, Rawh ibn al-Qasim, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab.
Ibn Abi Umar reported this through Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam with the same chain. The reports of Malik and Rawh are more complete and detailed.

Ibn Umar reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab gave a horse in the path of Allah, later found it for sale, and wanted to buy it. He asked the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Do not buy it and do not take back your charity.”

This account is reported through several chains: Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh from al-Layth; al-Muqaddami and Ibn al-Muthanna from Yahya al-Qattan; Ibn Numayr from his father; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah from Abu Usamah. They report from Ubayd Allah, Nafi, and Ibn Umar with wording like Malik’s report.

Umar gave a horse in the path of Allah and later saw it being sold, so he wanted to buy it. He asked the Prophet, who said: “Do not take back your charity, Umar.” The chain is Ibn Abi Umar and Abd ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Razzaq, Maamar, al-Zuhri, Salim, and Ibn Umar, who reported it from Umar.

Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet said: “The one who takes back his charity is like a dog that vomits, then returns to its vomit and eats it.” The chain is Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Razi and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Isa ibn Yunus, al-Awzai, Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, Ibn al-Musayyib, and Ibn Abbas.
This report is transmitted through Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Awzai, and Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, with wording similar to the preceding report.

This report comes through another chain: Hajjaj ibn al-Shair, Abd al-Samad, Harb, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr. It has wording similar to the preceding narrations. The chain is Hajjaj ibn al-Shair, Abd al-Samad, Harb ibn Shaddad, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, from Muhammad, son of Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger.

The Prophet said: “One who takes back a gift is like a dog that vomits and then eats its vomit.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar transmitted it from Shubah, Qatadah, Said ibn al-Musayyib, and Ibn Abbas. Harun ibn Said al-Ayli and Ahmad ibn Isa transmitted this from Ibn Wahb, Amr ibn al-Harith, Bukayr, Said ibn al-Musayyib, and Ibn Abbas.

This is the same report from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Ibn Abi Adi, Said, and Qatadah, through the same chain. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Jafar, Shubah, Qatadah, Said ibn al-Musayyib, and Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Abbas reported from the Messenger of Allah: “One who takes back a gift is like a dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit.” The chain includes Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, al-Makhzumi, Wuhaib, Abdullah ibn Tawus, and his father.

Al-Numan ibn Bashir said his father brought him to the Messenger of Allah and said, “I have given this son of mine a servant.” The Messenger asked whether he had given each child the same. When he said no, the Messenger said, “Then take it back.” Yahya ibn Yahya transmitted it from Malik and Ibn Shihab.

Al-Numan ibn Bashir said his father brought him to the Messenger of Allah and said he had given him a servant. The Prophet asked whether he had given the same to all his sons. When his father said no, the Prophet told him to take it back. This chain includes Yahya ibn Yahya and Ibrahim ibn Sad from Ibn Shihab. The chain is Yahya ibn Yahya, Malik, Ibn Shihab, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, Muhammad ibn al-Numan, and al-Numan ibn Bashir.

Several chains report this account with different wording: some say “all your sons,” others “all your children.” Yunus and Maamar have the first wording; al-Layth and Ibn Uyaynah have the second. Al-Layth’s report says Bashir brought al-Numan.

Al-Numan ibn Bashir said his father gave him a servant. The Prophet asked whether his brothers had all received the same. When his father said no, he said, “Then return it.” Qutaybah ibn Said transmitted it from Jarir, Hisham ibn Urwah, and his father. This account comes by several chains: Ibn Uyaynah, al-Layth, Yunus, and Abd al-Razzaq, all reporting from al-Zuhri through the same chain. Their versions differ on whether the Prophet said “your sons” or “your children.”

Al-Numan ibn Bashir said: “My father gave me some of his property, but my mother Amrah bint Rawahah would not be satisfied until the Messenger of Allah witnessed it.” The Prophet asked whether his father had done this for all his children. When he said no, the Prophet said, “Be mindful of Allah and treat your children fairly.” His father then took the gift back.

Al-Numan said his mother asked his father to give him a gift. His father delayed for a year, then agreed, but she insisted that the Messenger witness it. The Prophet asked whether he had given the same to all his children. When he said no, the Prophet said, “Do not ask me to witness this, for I will not witness injustice.” Al-Numan said his father gave him some of his property. His mother, Amrah bint Rawahah, would not agree until the Messenger witnessed the gift. His father went to the Prophet, who asked whether he had done this for all his children. When he said no, the Prophet told them to fear Allah and be fair to their children; the father returned the gift.

The Prophet asked Bashir whether he had other sons and whether he gave each the same. Bashir said no. The Prophet said, “Then do not ask me to witness injustice.” The report is transmitted through Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Yahya ibn Yahya from al-Shabi. Al-Numan said that his mother, bint Rawahah, asked his father to give some of his property to her son. The father delayed for a year, then decided to do so. She said she would not be satisfied until he had the Messenger of Allah witness the gift. His father took the young al-Numan by the hand to the Prophet and explained that his mother wanted this witnessed. The Prophet asked whether Bashir had any other children and whether he had given all of them the same. Bashir said no. The Prophet replied, “Then do not ask me to witness it, for I will not bear witness to injustice.” The report is transmitted by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr through Ali ibn Mushir, Abu Hayyan, al-Shabi, and al-Numan.

The Messenger of Allah asked al-Numan’s father whether he had other sons and gave them all the same. When the father said no, the Messenger said, “I will not witness injustice.” Ibn Numayr transmitted it from his father and Ismail, from al-Shabi.
The Prophet told al-Numan’s father: “Do not ask me to witness injustice.” This report is transmitted by Ishaq ibn Ibrahim from Jarir and Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Shabi and al-Numan ibn Bashir.

Al-Numan ibn Bashir said his father took him to the Messenger to witness a gift. The Prophet asked whether all his sons received the same and whether he wanted them equally dutiful to him. The father said yes. The Prophet replied, “Then do not do that.” The report is transmitted through Ibn Ulayyah, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and al-Shabi. The report comes through Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Abd al-Wahhab and Abd al-Ala; and through Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Yaqub al-Dawraqi from Ibn Ulayyah. Yaqub wording is given. Ismail ibn Ibrahim, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and al-Shabi transmit it from al-Numan ibn Bashir.

Al-Numan ibn Bashir said his father gave him a gift and took him to the Messenger as a witness. The Prophet asked whether all his children received the same and whether he wanted equal kindness from them. His father said yes; the Prophet said, “Then I will not witness it.” Ibn Awn recalled the wording, “Keep your children on equal terms.” Al-Numan ibn Bashir said his father gave him a gift and brought him to the Messenger to witness it. The Prophet asked whether he had given every child the same and whether he wanted equal kindness from them. When he said yes, the Prophet said he would not witness it. Ibn Awn said he related this to Muhammad, who recalled the wording: “Keep your children on equal terms.” The chain includes Ahmad ibn Uthman, Azhar, Ibn Awn, al-Shabi, and al-Numan.

Jabir reported that Bashir’s wife asked him to give their son his servant and have the Messenger witness it. The Prophet asked whether the boy had brothers and whether they all received the same. Bashir said no. The Prophet said, “That is not right, and I will witness only what is just.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus transmitted this from Zuhayr, Abu al-Zubayr, and Jabir. Bashir wife asked him to give her son his servant and have the Messenger witness it. The Prophet asked whether the boy had brothers and whether he had given them all the same. Bashir said no. The Prophet said this was not right and that he would witness only what was just.

Jabir ibn Abdullah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “Any man who gives a lifetime grant to someone and that person’s descendants, it belongs to the recipient and will not return to the giver, because it is a gift subject to inheritance.”
